title: Agent Braid ownership declaration (draft, not adopted)
description: Vendor-neutral declaration of what each parallel unit reads, writes, creates and deletes, written by the orchestrator. It is a claim, not an observation. It carries paths and class labels only: no file content, command text, prompt or transcript member exists. The surface member is drawn from the closed four-id vocabulary of the whole orchestration family; adding a surface is a versioned schema change.

base.description: The base the declaration was written against. Required when any unit claims completeness. A branch or tag name is resolved and pinned by the expansion step; a full commit identifier is used as is.

provenance.description: Who wrote the declaration. For an imported declaration the importing tool and its version are named in importedFrom (rendered imported:<tool>@<version>); an imported declaration is an input to the analyzer, never authority and never a grant.

importedFrom.description: Present only when provenance is imported. Names the other coordination tool and the dated version whose output format was verified. No adapter ships in the first releases.

unattributedWriterExemptions.description: Explicit, declared exemption rules. Writers that cannot be attributed to a unit (orchestrator, human, shared tree) are reported as unknown by default; only a path covered by a rule here is excluded from that report, and the receipt names the rule. A rule never attributes a write to a unit and never marks a write safe.

path.description: A repository-relative or absolute path, directory or glob pattern. The expansion step normalizes it; the schema only bounds it.

id.description: Unit id. The word unattributed is reserved for the attributed-write export and is refused.

surface.description: Closed vocabulary shared by the whole orchestration family: dynamic-workflow tracks, sessions launched from another session, agent teams sharing one working tree, and /batch units.

criticalReads.description: Reads whose content the unit depends on. A write by another unit to one of these is a hazard, not an advisory overlap. Every entry must also be covered by reads; this is checked by the validator, not by the schema.

dependsOn.description: Declared dependencies on other unit ids. They are the only source of the analyzer class ordered.

complete.description: True only if the orchestrator states that the reads, writes, creates and deletes are complete. Even then, coverage is partial unless every entry expands exactly.
